subject: SLO gate alignment — Velox Media perf qualification & MAP

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: SLO gate alignment — Velox Media perf qualification & MAP

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + proposed mutual action plan so we have an aligned SLO fence before the POC.

Summary of what we heard (please flag any corrections):
- Target serving mode: streaming (chunked responses to client) for user-facing search results.
- Latency target: 200 ms P95 for 256-token responses when streaming; 90% of production queries are <= 128 tokens.
- Concurrency requirement: support 500 concurrent active sessions during peak (burst to 750).
- Throughput: roughly 1.2M tokens / day (expected growth to ~1.8M).
- Acceptance criteria for canary: sustained P95 <= 220 ms across a 10k request/10-minute synthetic window with <0.5% error rate.

Open constraints you mentioned: on-prem sandbox for data locality (priors: logs must not leave VPC), budget cap for monthly inference costs, and preferred cloud region us-west-2.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood provides: SLO checklist + canary config (attached), perf test harness (perf-probe.sh) and a recommended initial canary workload by EOD Wed.
2) Velox: provide representative sample traffic (anonymized) and confirm whether streaming must be SSE or WebSocket.
3) Schedule whitebox lab run with Ben (SE) to run the canary: target window next Tue (12/8) — 90 min.
4) Post-canary: Redwood will produce a short decision brief with latency percentiles, token cost estimates, and suggested batching/quantization levers.

Acceptance decision criteria (to confirm):
- P95 latency target met (<= 220 ms) during canary
- No sustained tail spikes > 500 ms
- Token cost estimate within agreed budget threshold (TBD in step 2)

Attachments: velox-slo-checklist.pdf (SLO matrix), redwood-canary-config.yaml, perf-probe.sh (shell harness).

If that looks right, I’ll push the canary config and a proposed slot for the lab run.

Thanks — Markus

Thanks Markus — this is a solid recap. A couple of clarifications from our side before we commit the sample traffic: 

- Streaming protocol: we prefer SSE for browser clients but use a WS fallback for integrations. SSE is the default ask.
- Budget: cap of $35k/month for inference during the pilot (includes streaming tokens and dedicated capacity).
- Data locality: the sandbox can be a VPC peering arrangement; logs must remain in our account and be accessible for 90 days.

Two questions on the acceptance criteria:
1) For the canary window, does Redwood count client-side aggregation latency (e.g., JS merge time) or purely server-side end-to-end RTT to first partial chunk?
2) Can you provide an estimate for the expected cold-start penalty for a 1-2 minute idle cycle? We want to know if 500 concurrent during a burst will cause JVM-like cold starts.

I'll pull together an anonymized 48-hour sample and share a signed NDA if you still need one for the VPC arrangement.

— Alex

Alex — quick technical notes / answers to your two questions: 

1) Measurement boundary: Redwood will report server-side server-to-first-chunk RTT (we instrument at the reverse proxy and at the model runtime to compute P50/P95/P99 server-side). Client-side aggregation time is outside the canary acceptance metric but we’ll capture a small client-side probe during the lab run to show delta.

2) Cold-starts: for the model variant we discussed (8-bit quantized medium), cold-start median penalty is ~300-350 ms on our standard Dedicated pool; 95th percentile cold start can spike to ~700 ms if the node has to pull weights from secondary storage. For the canary we recommend keeping a warm pool with min-instances=2 per node-pool to avoid those large spikes — that’s in the attached redwood-canary-config.yaml (see warm_pool.min_instances).

Suggested metrics to capture during the lab run (we will push dashboards):
- Server P50/P95/P99 to first chunk
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) and aggregate tokens/day extrapolation
- Tail error rate and streaming stall events (stalls defined as >150 ms gap between chunks)
- KV cache hit ratio for repeated prefixes
- Memory/GPU utilization and GC/paging events

I’ll attach a quick perf probe (perf-probe.sh) you can run in your sandbox to replicate the 256-token streaming pattern. For the lab run, Ben will lead instrumentation and Markus will own the decision brief. Monica will coordinate billing/contract boundaries.

We can run the lab Tuesday 12/8 10:00–11:30 PT if that works.

– Ben

All — thanks for the quick replies and the constraints. Confirming updated MAP and owners/timeline below.

Agreed items:
- Streaming protocol: SSE primary, WS fallback — Velox confirms.
- Budget: pilot cap $35k/month — marked in the MAP (Monica to own billing threshold).
- Measurement: Redwood will report server-side P95 to first-chunk; client probe will be captured as a delta.
- Warm pool recommendation accepted: min-instances=2 (Ben to provision in canary config).

Mutual action plan (finalized):
- 12/3 (this week): Velox to upload anonymized 48-hour sample and sign the sandbox addendum (Alex / Priya).
- 12/6: Redwood uploads finalized canary config + perf script (Markus).
- 12/8, 10:00–11:30 PT: Lab canary run (Ben leads instrumentation; Velox to provide network access).
- 12/9: Redwood decision brief (latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, suggested levers) — Markus deliverable.
- 12/10: Joint decision checkpoint — approval to proceed to trial or iterate on config.

Fallbacks / gating rules: if P95 > 300 ms or error rate > 1% during canary, we will hold on rollout and run a follow-up iteration (tuning batching, KV cache, or quantization).

Next immediate actions:
- Alex/Priya: upload sample + NDA / sandbox addendum to the HubSpot link (I pasted below).
- Monica: confirm billing contact and create a billing threshold in the trial order (Monica will coordinate via the procurement channel).
